record.paper_title: Bootstrap Algebraic Multigrid: status report, open problems, and outlook
record.original_question: Given a current set C of coarse variables for bootstrap algebraic multigrid, how should one choose the initial coarse set C0 and then make local additions, removals, or other modifications to C whenever compatible relaxation converges too slowly, so that the updated coarse space improves convergence without introducing unnecessary complexity?

evidence.quote: How to choose C0 and how to identify suitable local modifications to a given set of coarse variables whenever the CR convergence rate is slow?

there is still no rigorous understanding of or justification for using pointwise errors of CR to determine the variables that will most effectively reduce the convergence rate of the CR process when added to C.
An efficient mechanism for updating coarse variable set C based on a local slowness of CR relaxation, see Section 2;

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a sparse linear system $A u = f$ where $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is a symmetric positive definite matrix arising, e.g., from the discretization of a partial differential equation on a fine index set $\Omega = \{1,\dots,n\}$. A two-level algebraic multigrid method partitions $\Omega = C \cup F$ into a coarse set $C$ and a fine-only set $F$, and uses an interpolation operator $P$ from $\mathbb{R}^{|C|}$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$ together with a smoother $M$ (so that $A = M + M^\top - M^\top D^{-1} M$ for some splitting). 

Compatible relaxation (CR). Given $C \subset \Omega$ with complementary set $F$, let $A_{ff}$ denote the principal submatrix of $A$ on $F$, and let $M_{ff}$ be the corresponding restriction of the smoother. The CR iteration on $F$ is
$$ e^{(k+1)}_F = (I - M_{ff}^{-1} A_{ff})\, e^{(k)}_F, \qquad e^{(k)}_C \equiv 0, $$
and its asymptotic convergence factor is
$$ \rho_{cr}(C) := \rho\bigl(I - M_{ff}^{-1} A_{ff}\bigr). $$
A small $\rho_{cr}(C)$ indicates that $C$ is a good candidate coarse set in the sense that an accurate two-level method can be built on it.

Problem. Design and justify, in a way that is independent of any a priori notion of strength of connection, an algorithm that:

1. Constructs an initial coarse set $C_0 \subset \Omega$ from the matrix $A$ (and possibly a small number of test vectors approximating the algebraically smooth error of $A$), together with a quantitative criterion guaranteeing that $\rho_{cr}(C_0)$ is bounded by a prescribed target $\rho^\star \in (0,1)$ when such a set of bounded size $|C_0| \le \kappa n$ exists.

2. Given a current coarse set $C$ for which $\rho_{cr}(C) > \rho^\star$, prescribes local modifications to $C$ — additions of indices from $F$, removals of indices from $C$, or other local updates — using only locally measurable quantities derived from CR (such as pointwise components of the slowly converging CR error, or local residual quantities), so that the updated set $C'$ satisfies $\rho_{cr}(C') < \rho_{cr}(C)$ while controlling the growth of $|C'|$ and of the resulting operator complexity.

3. Provides a rigorous justification that the local CR-based indicators used in step 2 (e.g., pointwise magnitudes of the slow CR error) actually identify the variables whose addition to $C$ most effectively decreases $\rho_{cr}$, i.e., proves quantitative bounds relating these local indicators to the resulting decrease in the CR convergence rate.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to choose the initial coarse set and how to perform CR-driven local updates remains an active area. Subsequent works (e.g., Brannick–Falgout's CR-based coarsening, relaxation-corrected bootstrap AMG, and least angle regression coarsening for BAMG) propose heuristic algorithms and partial analyses, but no rigorous justification has been established showing that pointwise CR errors identify the variables whose addition optimally reduces the CR convergence rate. The problem appears still open in its rigorous form.

status_evidence.title: Compatible Relaxation and Coarsening in Algebraic Multigrid
status_evidence.snippet: A coarsening algorithm for AMG based on compatible relaxation that does not rely on any notion of strength of connection.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a CR-based coarsening procedure but framed as a heuristic algorithm, not a rigorous optimality proof.

status_evidence.title: Least Angle Regression Coarsening in Bootstrap Algebraic Multigrid
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes LARS-based coarsening within bootstrap AMG.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the coarse-set selection question is still being addressed via new heuristics post-2014.

status_evidence.title: Optimal interpolation and Compatible Relaxation in Classical Algebraic Multigrid
status_evidence.snippet: Studies optimal interpolation and CR in classical AMG.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent research continues to investigate CR-based coarse-set selection without a closed answer.

status_evidence.title: Relaxation-corrected bootstrap algebraic multigrid (rBAMG)
status_evidence.snippet: Modifies the BAMG framework with relaxation correction.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates ongoing modifications to BAMG coarsening, suggesting the original question remains open.
